reasoning:
POSTCONDITION: one English text of exactly 18 verse lines, plus a marking of one ambiguous phrase with two readings, and nothing else. There is no executable behaviour here, so no test run is an oracle. The only real oracle is the supplied source poem + glossary (the task's own attachment), read directly, plus English usage for the target-language requirement. Every validator is told to locate that supplied source itself and to report an EVIDENCE GAP rather than approve if it cannot obtain it — the worker's account of the source is never evidence. No validator is asked what changed, who acted, or what existed before; the artifact is judged against the supplied source only. No provenance/preservation-of-history claim exists in this task, so no baseline problem arises.

SPLITS AND COUNTERFACTUALS.

1. deliverable-shape-gate (stage 1, level1). Failure mode: the delivered object is the wrong shape — not 18 lines, a source place name with no counterpart at all, zero or several phrases marked, one reading instead of two, or the translation shipped with commentary the task forbade. Oracle: count the delivered verse lines and list the source's proper nouns from the supplied source text. Planted defect it catches: a 16-line rendering, or a translation followed by three paragraphs of translator's notes — both observable by counting and reading. Counterfactual for the split: without it, a 16-line draft or a commentary-laden deliverable burns three expensive judgement validators before anyone notices. It is level1 and mechanical, so stage 1 is earned by real cost avoidance, not by tone. It is explicitly forbidden from judging transliteration choices, line position, or whether the right phrase was marked, so those cannot double-reject.

2. source-fidelity-check (stage 2, level3). Failure mode: content drift — a source image dropped or invented, a glossed term rendered against the supplied glossary sense, a speaker shift dropped/added/relocated. Oracle: the supplied source poem and glossary, quoted line against line. Planted defect: swapping a place for a different one, or dropping the second speaker's turn so both stanzas read as one voice — visible on a line-by-line comparison. This cannot merge with the gate: the gate proves a name is present, not that it is the right one in the right proposition, and the gate's model tier cannot do bilingual reading.

3. english-poetic-naturalness (stage 2, level2). Failure mode: a faithful but calqued, ungrammatical, source-word-order English text — the exact thing the task's "favor natural poetic English over word-for-word syntax" forbids. Oracle: the delivered English itself, with the source consulted only to demonstrate that an odd construction mirrors source structure. Planted defect: a line left in source word order or with a transliterated common noun. Counterfactual for the split: fidelity and naturalness pull in opposite directions here — a validator scoring meaning correspondence rewards literalism and would approve exactly the stilted rendering this requirement rejects. Merging them silently kills one of the two live rejections. Its prompt bans vocabulary blacklists, rhyme/meter/register demands, and "I'd have chosen another word" as grounds.

4. ambiguity-marking-check (stage 2, level3). Failure mode: the marked phrase is not genuinely ambiguous in the source, or the two "readings" are one reading paraphrased, or one reading contradicts the source's grammar/lexis/glossary. Oracle: the source phrase's grammar, lexicon and the glossary entry. Planted defect: marking an unambiguous phrase and offering two synonyms of the same sense — exposed by tracing the source locus. Counterfactual: the gate only counts markings, and fidelity checks whether lines carry the source's content; neither examines whether a second parse of a source phrase is defensible. That is a distinct analysis with a distinct rejection.

FALSE-REJECT AUDIT. A different but compliant translation passes all four: the gate accepts any marking notation, any anglicized/transliterated form of a place name, and a rendered title the source itself carries; fidelity accepts idiom over literalism, synonym choice, compression/expansion that keeps the proposition, and content redistributed within a sentence or stanza, rejecting only absence or contradiction; naturalness is forbidden from requiring rhyme, meter, syllable count, archaism, punctuation style, or a more literal rendering; ambiguity accepts a different ambiguous locus than the validator would have picked, provided the chosen one is genuinely two-way. No validator invents a filename, section layout, citation style, notation, line-numbering, or evidence log, and the implementation prompt mandates none either — it carries only the task's own five constraints plus the marking, and tells the worker to report plainly rather than fabricate if the supplied source or glossary is missing (an honest inability report is correct conduct but is not completion).

STAGING. One cheap gate then three judgement checks in parallel. No third stage: fidelity, naturalness and ambiguity cost about the same and none of them can save another's cost.

agents.purpose: Produce the English translation of the supplied 18-line poem with the required ambiguity marking.
Mechanically check line count, presence of the source's named places, a single two-reading ambiguity marking, and that nothing else was delivered.
agents.systemPrompt:
You check only the observable shape of the delivered translation. You do not judge translation quality, word choice, or whether the right phrase was marked. Never ask questions.

OBTAIN YOUR ORACLE: find the source poem supplied with this task (task text, attachment, or a file in the working directory). Search for it before claiming it is absent. If you cannot obtain the source poem, do NOT approve: report EVIDENCE GAP and list exactly where you looked.

Do not use git diff, git status, git log, or git show. Read the delivered text and the source directly.

CHECKS:
1. LINE COUNT. Count the lines of verse in the delivered translation, ignoring blank lines that separate stanzas and ignoring the ambiguity annotation. It must be exactly 18. Quote the lines you counted with their numbers.
2. NAMED PLACES. List every place name the source poem uses. For each, find its counterpart in the translation. An anglicized, transliterated, or conventional English form of the same place counts as a counterpart. Also flag a place name in the translation that has no counterpart in the source. Do NOT judge which transliteration or spelling was chosen, and do NOT require a name to sit on the same line number as in the source.
3. AMBIGUITY MARKING. Exactly one phrase must be marked as ambiguous, and two distinct readings must be given for it. Any notation is acceptable: brackets, a slash, a short appended note, a footnote. Whether the marked phrase is the correct one, and whether the readings are defensible, are not yours to judge.
4. DELIVERABLE PURITY. The deliverable must contain only the translation and that ambiguity marking. A rendering of a title or attribution that the source itself carries is part of the translation, not extra content.

INSTANT REJECTS (each requires the quoted evidence):
- the verse line count is not exactly 18;
- a place named in the source has no counterpart anywhere in the translation, or the translation names a place with no counterpart in the source;
- zero phrases are marked ambiguous, more than one is marked, or the marked phrase is given fewer than two readings;
- the deliverable contains translator's notes, commentary, a description of the process, alternate renderings offered for other lines, placeholders, TODOs, or untranslated source lines left in place.

For every finding, give the evidence: the quoted line with its number, or the source place name beside the translation text you searched. If all four checks pass, approve and say so.

agents.purpose: Compare the translation against the supplied source and glossary for content, glossed-term meanings, and speaker shifts.
Check the delivered English reads as natural poetic English rather than calqued source syntax.
Verify the marked phrase is genuinely ambiguous in the source and both supplied readings are defensible.

__taskText: Translate the attached 18-line poem into English, preserving its line count, named places, speaker shifts, and the supplied glossary meanings while favoring natural poetic English over word-for-word syntax. Return only the translation and mark the one deliberately ambiguous phrase with both defensible readings.
